outcome: A June 2026 preprint by Kothari and Tudose (arXiv:2606.12197) claims a full proof of Brouwer's conjecture by establishing an equivalence between the conjecture and the (previously proven) Grone-Merris-Bai theorem, restricted via split graphs; as of the research date (2026-09-22, about 3.5 months after posting) no expert digestion, journal acceptance, or independent verification has been found, and a July 2026 follow-up (arXiv:2607.03388) that builds directly on it to resolve the equality-case question (Li-Guo's 'full Brouwer conjecture') has likewise not been digested.

ai.basis_quote: We used GPT 5.5 Pro to simplify our proof that Brouwer's Inequality implies the Grone-Merris-Bai theorem. We also used it for a proofreading of our manuscript.

summary: The triage's pointer checks out on the facts but the classification needs tightening. Kothari and Tudose (arXiv:2606.12197, posted 2026-06-10) claim a full proof of Brouwer's conjecture on Laplacian eigenvalue sums, via an equivalence with the Grone-Merris-Bai theorem restricted to split graphs. I read the full HTML rendering of the paper: it is short (about 13-14 pages), has no acknowledgements section but does carry an explicit 'Statement of AI Use' reading verbatim 'We used GPT 5.5 Pro to simplify our proof that Brouwer's Inequality implies the Grone-Merris-Bai theorem. We also used it for a proofreading of our manuscript.' That is a disclosed, author-stated contribution of a specific named system to part of the mathematical content (simplifying one direction of the core equivalence), not merely proofreading, so I coded ai_role as assisted rather than none, with basis_quote and source as required. As of the research date (2026-09-22), roughly 3.5 months after posting, I found no expert digestion (no Terence Tao blog post, no MathOverflow thread, no journal acceptance notice), so the paper remains unverified by the mathematical community at large and status is claimed, not resolved. A July 2026 follow-up (arXiv:2607.03388, Cai/Chen/Yang/Zhang, v2 dated 2026-08-10) explicitly builds on the Kothari-Tudose proof ('Motivated by their perfect proof and methods...') to settle the equality-case characterization conjectured by Li and Guo (2022); it carries no AI-use statement of its own. I found no retraction, withdrawal, or identified error specific to the Kothari-Tudose paper itself, though I did find (via search snippets referencing an AI-review platform, Pith Review, at pith.science) that other, unrelated 2025-2026 preprints attempting partial proofs of Brouwer's conjecture were flagged with logical gaps by that automated reviewer -- those are different papers, not the Kothari-Tudose one, and I could not get Pith Review's page content to load to confirm whether it has reviewed 2606.12197 at all. Given the short elapsed time and the paper's brevity for such a major claim, I rate confidence medium: the mathematical claim is plausible and well-cited by fast-moving follow-up work, but the field has not yet had the years typical of digesting a 50-year-old conjecture's resolution.
competing_reading: One could argue ai_role should be 'none': the disclosed GPT contribution was to 'simplify' an already-established implication (Brouwer's Inequality implies GMB) rather than to originate new mathematical content, which is arguably closer to proofreading/tidying than to producing an argument, case, or bound that wasn't already there. I coded it as assisted because 'simplify our proof' is a step beyond pure proofreading -- it implies the model reworked part of the argument's presentation or structure, which is different from spell-checking prose -- but a stricter reading that requires the AI to have supplied genuinely new mathematical content (not just restructured existing content) would move this to 'none'. Separately, status could arguably stay 'open' rather than 'claimed' if one takes the view that a completely undigested, un-refereed, 13-page resolution of a 50-year-old conjecture with a short elapsed window carries too little epistemic weight to register as anything beyond noise; I judged 'claimed' more appropriate since the paper unambiguously exists, makes the claim in scope, and has already drawn serious follow-up work from other named mathematicians who treat it as correct.
what_would_settle_it: An expert digestion (e.g., a referee report, journal acceptance, or a post by a recognized spectral-graph-theory expert such as Terence Tao's blog or a MathOverflow thread) confirming or refuting the Kothari-Tudose argument would settle status between claimed and resolved (or reveal a gap making it open/open_stale-adjacent). Getting Pith Review's or another automated/human reviewer's assessment specifically of arXiv:2606.12197 (not just of unrelated Brouwer-conjecture preprints) would also help. For the ai_role classification, seeing the actual before/after text of the 'simplified' proof step, or an author interview/talk describing what GPT 5.5 Pro changed, would clarify whether it contributed novel mathematical content or only restructured existing human-derived content.
